geometry_edits.rationale: Deepen the access-side notch to strengthen the public threshold without changing the dominant anchor.
Widen the carve so the frontage reads as an entry seam or court-like void.
Extend the notch vertically so the ground response registers across more of the mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Deepen the access-side subtraction so the west-facing threshold reads more clearly in plan and elevation.
Broaden the opening to create a more usable public seam rather than a thin edge nick.
Carry the entry cut farther through section so the access response is legible as a spatial gesture.

rationale: The mass is coherent across all four views and the dominant object remains readable as one compact neighborhood-scale building, so it avoids the one-view-only failure. The profiled footprint helps slightly with parcel response, but the form mostly behaves like a generic rectangular extrusion with a small chamfered/top notch rather than a clearly authored public mass. The verified access edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no strong court, undercut, or entry seam that materially opens toward the frontage. Hierarchy is acceptable, but the void/public-space figure is underdeveloped, and the section reads more like a simple capped box than a program-rich living/community threshold. References point toward the needed direction: a clearer carved void or notch, stronger street-facing public ground condition, and a calm but more legible upper mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and materially articulated; the candidate is simpler and more boxy, so only the spatial void logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise massing with a legible central void and a clear upper-level connector can support neighborhood/community programs well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a larger multi-building complex; copying its aggregation would over-fragment this small candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, courtyard-based campus composition shows how multiple masses can organize shared public space without losing hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate has only a shallow notch and little visible public-room effect, so the reference is aspirational rather than matched.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong recessed cut or undercut at ground level can activate the street edge while keeping the primary volume calm.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not yet show the clearer lateral spread or sectional richness of the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low elongated mass with a courtyard/atrium void and a slightly folded roof can read as neighborhood-use architecture.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference has a more pronounced multi-wing organization; the candidate remains a single compact block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connecting circulation and a central void can create an active neighborhood public sequence while preserving a dominant mass.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the rendered views, but the geometry is close to simply filling the available envelope.
The access edge response is too sealed and semantically neutral for neighborhood_living; it needs a more legible public threshold.
The silhouette is not invalid, but it is still closer to an ordinary stepped/boxed mass than to a spatially consequential neighborhood figure.
